2.2.2.1-f46.text: Catullum ad Ipsithillam, &c. Ovid. Eleg. lib. 3 & 6, &c. Quot itinera una nocte confecissent tot coronas ludicro deo puta Triphallo, Marsiae, Hermae, Priapo donarent, Cingemus tibi mentulam coronis, &c

translations.note: 'Itinera' (journeys) is a euphemism for sexual bouts. Catullus's poem to Ipsithilla is the one boasting of nine bouts in a row. Burton's Ovid reference is presumably to the Amores. 'Cingemus tibi mentulam coronis' is a Priapic-style hendecasyllable, and its source is not certain.

translations.text: Catullus to Ipsithilla, etc. Ovid, Elegies book 3 & 6, etc. As many journeys as they had made in one night, so many garlands they would give to the sportive god, namely Triphallus, Marsyas, Hermes, Priapus: We will wreathe your member with garlands, etc.
